seoDescription: Learn how to build a simple punchbag game using Vue.js 2 by combining template structure, CSS styling, data properties, methods, and dynamic bindings. This tutorial walks through creating the bag image, health bar, controls, Vue data (health, ended), methods (punch, restart), v-bind for styles and classes, and conditional rendering to show a burst image when health reaches zero.

chapters.title: Introduction and Project Goal
chapters.description: Presenter introduces the tutorial objective: build a small punch bag game to bring together previously learned Vue.js basics.

chapters.title: Game Concept and Assets
chapters.description: Explains the punch bag game mechanics, assets used (bag and burst images), and where to find them in the repository.

chapters.title: HTML Template Structure
chapters.description: Builds the HTML layout: bag image div, bag health container with inner bar, and game controls with two buttons.

chapters.title: Styling the Bag Image
chapters.description: Adds CSS for the bag container: size, centered margin, background image, positioning, and background sizing to display the bag graphic.

chapters.title: Health Bar Styling and Behavior
chapters.description: Styles the health container and inner red bar, explains plan to reduce width from 100% to 0% as punches occur.

chapters.title: Controls Styling and Vue Instance Setup
chapters.description: Styles control buttons and begins populating the Vue instance with data, methods, and computed placeholders; adds initial Health data property.

chapters.title: Punch and Restart Methods
chapters.description: Implements punch and restart methods to decrement health by 10 and reset health to 100, and wires buttons to these methods with v-on:click.

chapters.title: Game End State and Conditional UI
chapters.description: Adds an 'ended' data property to track game completion, sets it true when health <= 0, resets it on restart, and conditionally shows the punch button using v-show with negation.

chapters.title: Dynamic Health Width, Burst Class Binding and Conclusion
chapters.description: Binds health bar width to health with v-bind:style, applies a 'burst' class to the bag when ended is true using v-bind:class to swap the image, and wraps up the demo.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Template structure**: separate the UI into clear elements — a bag image (#bag), a health container (#bag-health with inner bar), and controls (#controls) with buttons for actions.

- **Styling images and layout**: use CSS background-image, background-position: center, background-repeat: no-repeat, and background-size to display bag and burst graphics. Center elements with margin: 0 auto.

- **Reactive data**: define **health** (number, starts at 100) and **ended** (boolean, starts false) in the Vue data object to represent game state.

- **Methods**: implement **punch()** to decrement health by 10 and check if health <= 0 to set ended = true; implement **restart()** to reset health = 100 and ended = false.

- **Event binding**: wire buttons using v-on:click to call punch and restart.

- **Dynamic styles**: bind the health bar width with v-bind:style to compute width: health + '%', so visual health matches data.

- **Conditional UI**: use v-show="!ended" to hide the punch button when the game ends and prevent negative health.

- **Class binding for state visuals**: use v-bind:class with an object { burst: ended } to toggle a CSS class that swaps the bag background to the burst image when ended is true.

> [!TIP] Keep UI, state, and behavior separated: CSS handles visuals, Vue data tracks state, and methods mutate state on user interaction.

> [!IMPORTANT] Always guard state changes (e.g., check health <= 0 after decrement) to avoid invalid values and to trigger transitions like game end.

> [!NOTE] This example uses simple numeric health steps and basic bindings which are ideal to learn Vue reactivity before moving to more complex game logic or animations.
